qs.q: A neonate born with severe ventriculomegaly undergoes further neuroimaging to determine the exact structural cause prior to neurosurgery. What is a primary diagnostic advantage of fetal MRI over standard ultrasound in this evaluation?
o: It provides superior visualization of the underlying etiology
It allows continuous real-time bedside monitoring
It requires significantly less technician expertise
It eliminates all physiological scanning motion artifacts
qs.e: Magnetic resonance imaging offers superior visualization of the underlying etiology due to high soft-tissue resolution. Ultrasound, conversely, has lower resolution and is more operator-dependent.
qs.s: Congenital Hydrocephalus: Prenatal Diagnosis and Surgical: MCQs

qs.q: 63-year-old, known CAD, new harsh pansystolic murmur + cardiogenic shock 4 days after large inferior MI, severe MR on echo. MOST likely structural cause?
o: Left ventricular free wall rupture with pseudoaneurysm
Aortic root dilation causing aortic regurgitation
Rupture of the interventricular septum creating an acquired VSD
Papillary muscle rupture causing acute mitral valve incompetence
qs.e: - Inferior MIs (RCA territory) put the **posteromedial papillary muscle** (single blood supply) at high risk of rupture, causing acute severe MR — typically 3–7 days post-MI
qs.s: Cardiovascular Pathology MCQs: Rheumatic Fever, AAA, HTN, HFpEF
